reason: The context-sharing pitch fits my day — I run three agents and hate losing context when I switch tools. But my first thought was lock-in: if Loom shuts down, my context is trapped in its daemon. I evaluate launch-day tools constantly and most don't stick; I won't pay $30/seat to build my workflow on something I can't take with me.
objection: If Loom shuts down or gets acquired, my agents' shared sessions, skills, and credentials are locked in a local daemon I don't control.
would_change_my_mind: A portability guarantee — my sessions and skills live in open files I own and keep working without the daemon.
